name: Titoism
summary: Titoism is the doctrine and practice of the League of Communists of Yugoslavia under Josip Broz Tito after the 1948 break with Stalin. It replaced Soviet-style state ownership and central planning with social ownership, workers' self-management and market socialism, kept a one-party state that called itself socialist democracy, organized Yugoslavia as a federation of equal nations under 'brotherhood and unity', and pursued nonalignment between the Cold War blocs.
scope: The Yugoslav line from the 1948 split to Tito's death in 1980, as its defining sources present it: the 1958 Programme of the League of Communists (named by Benson's encyclopedia entry as the historic statement of 'self-governing socialism'), the 1974 constitution, the speeches of Tito and the theory of Edvard Kardelj, and the regime's record (McVicker 1957; the Library of Congress country study). It excludes the Stalinist 1945-48 phase except as background, the post-1980 republics' divergences, and foreign movements that borrowed the label.

keyFigures.role: Leader of the Yugoslav communists and of Yugoslavia from 1945 to 1980, after whom the doctrine is named.
The party's chief theoretician of self-management, under whose guidance the 1963 constitution was drafted.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The constitution organizes total national defence around the armed forces and the YPA.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Yugoslavia kept a central banking system, the National Bank and the republics' national banks, responsible for monetary policy (Library of Congress study).

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The constitution makes citizens equal regardless of social status and opens every function to all on equal terms.

abolish-ip.rationale: The constitution gives authors and inventors moral and material rights to their works.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The constitution regulates marriage by statute and requires it to be contracted before a competent agency.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The 1974 constitution calls for eliminating every form of wage-labour relationship, but the system kept money, markets and personal incomes paid by results.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The 1958 Programme calls the internal security organs an indispensable weapon of socialism while anti-socialist pressure lasts.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: The 1974 constitution calls for eliminating any form of wage-labour relationship.

abortion-legal.rationale: A liberalized abortion law was passed in 1969, free abortions were available up to ten weeks, and the 1974 constitution makes deciding on family planning a human right.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The 1958 Programme calls for mechanization on the largest possible scale, automation and the latest science in production.

alienated-labor.rationale: The 1974 constitution aims to end the alienation of workers from the means of production and the conditions of their labour.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: The constitution guarantees farmers ownership of arable land up to ten hectares.

allow-dual-citizenship.rationale: The constitution provides for Yugoslav citizens who also hold another citizenship.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The constitution founds the federation on the National Liberation War and Socialist Revolution against the fascist occupation.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The constitution makes profession of religion free and a private affair.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The constitution commits Yugoslavia to support peoples waging liberation wars against colonialism and oppression.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: The constitution forbids accepting occupation and makes armed struggle the decisive form of resisting aggression.

arms-reduction.rationale: The constitution commits Yugoslavia to general and complete disarmament.

automate-paid-work.rationale: The constitution names a reduction in working hours through technical progress among the aims of the system.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: No party but the League of Communists was allowed, and the constitution forbids using freedoms to disrupt the socialist self-management order.

bound-labor.rationale: The 1974 constitution guarantees free choice of occupation and prohibits forced labour.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The constitution has the assemblies pass budgets and the federal budget's total fixed in agreement with the republic assemblies.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The 1958 Programme says the capitalist system is gradually declining while a socialist society is being born.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The 1958 Programme keeps the thesis that imperialism breeds war but holds that a new world war is no longer inevitable, and Kardelj argued that war's inevitability depends on the balance of forces.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The constitution declares artistic creation free but forbids using freedoms in ways that offend public morals.

central-planning.rationale: From 1950 the regime abandoned Stalinist central planning: planning was decentralized to communes and workers' councils and the centre set only general guidelines (Library of Congress study).

character-from-environment.rationale: The 1958 Programme holds that new production relations change the peasant's social nature and whole mentality.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The constitution entitles those unable to work to assistance from the social community.

civil-marriage.rationale: The constitution requires marriage to be contracted before a competent state agency, and the regime instituted civil marriage.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The constitution commits Yugoslavia to support peoples' struggles for liberation from colonialism and all national subjugation.

class-collaboration.rationale: The 1958 Programme rejects the reformist course of compromise between capitalists and workers and calls for class struggle in capitalist countries.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The 1958 Programme describes history as marked by class and national oppression and the working class as the main driving force of social progress.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The 1958 Programme names bureaucracy among the anti-socialist forces distorting socialism toward state capitalism and calls for continued struggle against them.

clerical-rule.rationale: The constitution separates religious communities from the state and makes abuse of religion for political purposes unconstitutional.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The 1958 Programme calls the very idea of changing frontiers by force to settle minority questions alien to the League.

collective-defense.rationale: Yugoslavia stayed out of all military alliances after the 1950s and refused to join NATO (Library of Congress study).

collective-farming.rationale: Forced collectivization in 1949-52 was abandoned and most land returned to private peasants, while the regime kept promoting socialist estates and cooperatives (Library of Congress study).

conscription.rationale: Military service was compulsory for all male citizens, with no alternative service and prison for those who refused (Library of Congress study).

constitutional-jury-trial.rationale: Trial by jury did not exist in Yugoslavia; lay judges elected by communes only partly filled the role (Library of Congress study).

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The 1958 Programme sets a scientific, materialist outlook on the world as an aim of education.

death-penalty.rationale: The 1974 constitution declares life inviolable but allows federal statute to provide capital punishment exceptionally for the gravest crimes.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Social services received an unusually large share of public spending for a country of Yugoslavia's means, and the constitution guarantees assistance to those unable to work (Library of Congress study).

decide-locally.rationale: From the 1950s the communes held all political authority not delegated to the federation or republics, including planning, utilities and supervision of enterprises (Library of Congress study).

defeat-communism.rationale: Titoism is a communist doctrine, and the 1958 Programme's goal is socialism and communism.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The 1958 Programme demands relations between states based on independence and full equality, condemning great-power hegemony.

delink-world-market.rationale: The regime integrated with the world economy in the 1960s, joining GATT, taking foreign loans and allowing foreign joint ventures (Library of Congress study).

democracy-best.rationale: The regime rejected multiparty democracy for a one-party state; voters chose only from closed candidate lists, and no open nomination emerged by 1990 (Library of Congress study).

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The 1958 Programme defines democracy by its social substance and dismisses formal bourgeois democracy as a monopoly of party leaderships.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The 1958 Programme calls Yugoslav people's government a dictatorship of the proletariat, a transition to the abolition of all classes, and the 1974 constitution calls self-management a form of it.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The constitution has the president elected by the federal assembly at a joint session, not by popular vote.

direct-votes.rationale: The 1974 constitution has working people decide through assemblies and referenda in their workplaces, local communities and communes, though federal laws were passed by delegates.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Tito backed the Algerian proposal for a UN-supervised referendum and the Programme wants disputes settled by the wishes of the people concerned.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The 1974 constitution makes citizens equal regardless of sex and gives everyone equal access to every job and function.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The 1958 Programme names communism, with abundance enabling 'from each according to his ability, to each according to his needs', as the final goal.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The 1958 Programme builds Yugoslav unity on the equality and brotherhood of its many peoples and minorities.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The constitution vests power in the working class and working people.

dominated-front.rationale: Tito co-founded the Nonaligned Movement of former colonies and denounced neocolonialism, though the movement opposed both blocs rather than the West alone (Library of Congress study).

duties-before-rights.rationale: The 1974 constitution says freedoms are realized through fulfilment of duties to all, are limited by the interests of the socialist community, and may not be used against the socialist order.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The constitution provided for a collective presidency elected by the assemblies to follow Tito.

economic-freedom.rationale: The 1958 Programme holds that freedom for all requires abolishing the freedom of oppressors and grows from socialist social relations, not capitalist economic liberty.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The regime opened to world trade, joining GATT and signing a commercial agreement with the EEC (Library of Congress study).

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The 1958 Programme demands equality of all peoples and minorities and rejects national privileges.

elective-rulers.rationale: The constitution has the president and the collective state presidency elected by the assembly, not succeeding by inheritance.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The 1958 Programme sees substantial possibilities for the UN to play a greater role and exert more authority in settling disputes, and Tito asked the 1960 General Assembly to make the UN universal.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Yugoslavia stayed outside both military blocs, refused NATO membership and would not accept foreign troops of either alliance on its soil (Library of Congress study).

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The 1974 constitution lists rights that may not be restricted and gives them judicial protection, but bars their use against the socialist order and the courts could not enforce rulings against the assembly.

equal-conscription.rationale: Conscription applied to all male citizens only (Library of Congress study).

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The 1974 constitution makes citizens equal in rights and duties regardless of nationality, race, sex, language, religion, education or social status.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The 1974 constitution distributes income on the principle 'to each according to his labour', and the Programme warns against absolute parity of incomes as well as excessive gaps.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Yugoslavia was constituted as a federation of equal nations and nationalities, and the constitution guarantees equal rights regardless of nationality.

ethnicity-statistics.rationale: Yugoslav censuses recorded the population by nationality (Library of Congress study).

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The 1958 Programme says Yugoslavia must make every effort to develop its power and raw-material resources.

experts-over-public.rationale: The 1974 constitution declares 'technocratic usurpation' contrary to the system, and was designed to limit the influence of professional enterprise managers in favour of self-managing workers (Library of Congress study).

filial-duty.rationale: The constitution binds children to care for parents in need, and a 1962 law set out the support owed to parents and relatives.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: In 1971 police and soldiers arrested hundreds of Croatian student leaders and the regime purged the movement seeking near-independence for Croatia (Library of Congress study).

force-without-un.rationale: The constitution commits Yugoslavia to the UN Charter, peaceful settlement of disputes and renunciation of force in international relations.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: A 1967 law let foreigners hold at most 49 percent of joint ventures with Yugoslav firms (Library of Congress study).

free-trade.rationale: The constitution commits Yugoslavia to the broadest and freest possible exchange of goods, and in the 1960s the regime cut tariffs and import restrictions and joined GATT (Library of Congress study).

free-trade-promotes-peace.rationale: The 1958 Programme says restrictions on the free exchange of goods by blocs deepen political contradictions, and economic cooperation serves peace.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The constitution makes citizens equal regardless of nationality, race, sex or religion and punishes propagating inequality.

future-generations.rationale: The constitution binds everyone to preserve nature and to use land and water so as to keep a healthy environment.

government-encourage-intercultural-conta.rationale: The 1958 Programme pledges to promote rapprochement, mutual understanding and joint management among the peoples of Yugoslavia.

gradual-change.rationale: The 1958 Programme holds that the working class will use revolutionary means where reaction blocks its way, while also saying society cannot skip stages.

harm-principle.rationale: The constitution forbids using freedoms against the socialist order or in ways that offend public morals, limits that go beyond preventing harm to others.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The state presidency held supreme command of the armed forces, but the government was elected by and answerable to the assembly.

human-decline-since-golden-age.rationale: The 1958 Programme sees history as progress toward socialism and communism.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The constitution distributes income according to labour and forbids anyone to appropriate the product of social labour on property grounds.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The 1958 Programme calls economic development the basis of new states' political independence, and Tito told the UN that colonial economic relations kept independence from being genuine.

indirect-election.rationale: The 1974 constitution replaced direct elections with indirect elections by delegates from workplaces, communities and sociopolitical organizations up to the Federal Assembly.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pensions came from compulsory social insurance based on reciprocity and solidarity in self-managing communities of interest.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The 1974 constitution grants rights to nations and nationalities as groups, including self-determination and the use of their own languages.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The 1958 Programme makes continued industrialization and modern production methods the core of economic policy.

informal-organisation.rationale: The 1958 Programme organizes political struggle through the League of Communists, the Socialist Alliance and the trade unions.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The 1958 Programme denies that bourgeois democracy suits every society and holds that forms of democracy vary with each country's conditions and traditions.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The constitution requires only the free consent of the spouses for marriage and makes citizens equal regardless of religion.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The 1958 Programme condemns Soviet hegemony over socialist states and upholds non-interference in the internal affairs of other states.

job-guarantee.rationale: The constitution guarantees the right to work and obliges those managing social resources to create conditions for it.

labour-priority-over-capital.rationale: The 1974 constitution aims to eliminate the antagonism between labour and capital in favour of free associated labour.

land-redistribution.rationale: The regime seized large estates and gave land to peasants, and in 1953 cut the legal limit on holdings to ten hectares to relieve peasant landlessness (Library of Congress study).

language-defines-nation.rationale: Serbs, Croats, Montenegrins and Muslims, sharing Serbo-Croatian, were recognized as separate nations (Library of Congress study).

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The constitution separates religious communities from the state and makes abuse of religion for political purposes unconstitutional, leaving law wholly secular.

leader-cult.rationale: The leadership redoubled efforts to promote Tito's cult of personality in the 1970s, and he awarded himself the Order of National Hero three times (Library of Congress study; Benson).

legal-duty-to-work.rationale: The constitution guarantees freedom to work and prohibits forced labour, denying only labour rights to those who will not work.

limit-growth.rationale: The regime pursued industrialization and high investment for rapid growth, recording one of the world's fastest growth rates in the late 1950s (Library of Congress study).

limit-population.rationale: From the mid-1960s the government actively supported family planning to control population growth, with a 1969 resolution expanding free programmes (Library of Congress study).

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Yugoslavia ran market socialism while the League of Communists kept its political monopoly (Library of Congress study).

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The regime gave markets more room than any other communist state (the 1965 reform) but kept social planning, and in 1974 Tito ended the market-socialism experiment by putting economic policy back under party control (Library of Congress study).

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The 1958 Programme holds that progress in political relations is bound up with progress in economic relations and that consciousness springs from social relations.

member-state-blocks-federal-overreach.rationale: From 1971 the republics and provinces gained a de facto veto over federal decisions (Library of Congress study).

military-guardian-role.rationale: Military influence in politics grew steadily from the 1970s, as the army stabilized the country in crises and warned it would not allow its dissolution (Library of Congress study).

minority-language-support.rationale: The constitution gives nationalities the right to use their languages before state agencies and to schooling in their own language.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The constitution gives Kosovo and Vojvodina autonomous province status, with substantially increased autonomy from 1974.

minority-veto.rationale: Democratic centralism bound every party member to majority decisions once taken (Library of Congress study).

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The communist-led constituent assembly dissolved the monarchy in November 1945 and founded the federal republic that Titoism governed (Library of Congress study).

moral-incentives.rationale: The 1974 constitution distributes income 'to each according to his labour', making material reward for work the basis of pay.

more-religion-public.rationale: The regime ran antireligious propaganda, banned church involvement in politics, education and social affairs, and kept practising believers out of good jobs (Library of Congress study).

multipolar-world.rationale: The 1958 Programme opposes division of the world into blocs and great-power hegemony, favouring independent states outside them.

nation-first.rationale: The 1958 Programme says the independence of Yugoslav foreign policy is opposed to selfishness and national exclusiveness and serves comprehensive cooperation between peoples.

national-church-status.rationale: The constitution separates all religious communities from the state without privileging any.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The constitution guarantees nationalities schooling in their own language and the free expression of their national culture.

national-mission.rationale: The constitution upholds every nation's right to choose its own social and political system by its own means.

national-resource-control.rationale: The constitution commits Yugoslavia to sovereign exploitation of national natural resources.

national-self-determination.rationale: The 1974 constitution rests the federation on each nation's right to self-determination and commits Yugoslavia to that right abroad.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The 1958 Programme commits the League to socialism and communism, not a third course.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The constitution makes armed defence of the country every citizen's supreme duty.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The constitution gives the social community duties in health, welfare, housing, education and planning far beyond defence and justice.

no-bailouts.rationale: Unprofitable enterprises were protected by the state until the 1990 reform exposed them to bankruptcy (Library of Congress study).

no-central-bank.rationale: Yugoslavia kept a central banking system led by the National Bank (Library of Congress study).

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The constitution makes abuse of religion for political purposes unconstitutional.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The constitution binds everyone to abide by the constitution and the law.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Yugoslav doctrine refused to accept foreign troops of either alliance on its territory under any threat or inducement (Library of Congress study).

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: The 1958 Programme demands a ban on the use and production of nuclear weapons and opposes foreign military bases.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Catholic schools were closed and religious instruction discouraged, the constitution allows religious schools only for training clergy, and the Programme calls for separating school from church.

no-transition-to-communism.rationale: The 1958 Programme describes a long transition period from capitalism through socialism to communism.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Tito headed both party and state, and the LCY president sat ex officio on the state presidency until 1988 (Library of Congress study).

one-party-rule.rationale: Through the 1980s Yugoslavia remained a one-party state: the League of Communists rejected multiparty pluralism and kept a monopoly of political organization (Library of Congress study).

organic-representation.rationale: The 1974 assemblies represent citizens through chambers of associated labour, local communities and sociopolitical organizations rather than competing parties.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The constitution makes the assemblies the bodies of power, and the Federal Assembly the highest expression of the self-management system.

parliamentary-road-socialism.rationale: The 1958 Programme holds that the working class in some countries can win power by comparatively peaceful and parliamentary means.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The constitution gives every working person the right to self-management in workplaces and local communities through assemblies, referenda and delegates.

party-commands-army.rationale: The constitution gives supreme command to the state presidency, though the party had a committee in the army and officers had to be members (Library of Congress study).

party-controls-media.rationale: All media needed the political sponsorship of the party-led socialist alliances, journalists had to belong to the party-controlled league, and publication boards ensured party control (Library of Congress study).

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Under democratic centralism, once the League made a final decision after free debate, it bound every member (Library of Congress study).

party-own-road.rationale: The 1958 Programme defends each socialist country's right to build socialism by its own road, and condemns the Cominform's attempt to impose Soviet hegemony in 1948.

patriotic-education.rationale: The 1958 Programme pledges to rear citizens, especially youth, in Yugoslav socialist patriotism and readiness to sacrifice everything for the country.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The 1958 Programme calls Yugoslav socialist patriotism the complement of internationalism and defence of the socialist fatherland every citizen's highest duty.

people-in-arms.rationale: Total National Defense armed the population in Territorial Defense Forces to supplement, not replace, the standing Yugoslav People's Army (Library of Congress study).

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The constitution vests authority in elected and recallable delegates and assemblies under statute, not personal bonds.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The constitution guarantees ownership of personal property for one's needs while the means of production are social property.

political-decisions-consensus.rationale: The 1974 system coordinated planning through social compacts and agreements that were consensual by definition (Library of Congress study).

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The 1958 Programme reports that Yugoslavia joined no regional economic organization because bloc and great-power influence shaped them.

population-transfer.rationale: The 1958 Programme says all national minorities enjoy full rights and that Yugoslav minority policy never depended on relations with neighbouring states.

positive-liberty.rationale: The 1958 Programme holds that human rights depend on a social and material foundation and that freedom cannot be achieved by an abstract formula.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The collective state presidency gave each republic and province equal seats, and nationality quotas shared posts in party, state and foreign service (Library of Congress study).

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The 1974 constitution guarantees every citizen the right to express their national culture and use their own language, though nationalist cultural bodies such as Matica Hrvatska were disbanded in 1971.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The regime set price controls at key points of production and reimposed them in 1974; even the 1990 reform kept controls on essentials (Library of Congress study).

price-controls-fight-inflation.rationale: In 1974, with Europe's highest inflation, the government reimposed the price controls relaxed in 1965 (Library of Congress study).

private-courts-defense.rationale: The constitution vests justice in courts of law and defence in the Yugoslav People's Army and the territorial defence of the whole people.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The 1958 Programme treats capitalist private ownership as a system of exploitation of the worker, which social ownership abolishes.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: The constitution upholds each nation's right to choose its own system and non-interference in others' internal affairs.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The constitution allows punishment only for acts defined by statute beforehand and by courts in procedures regulated by statute.

property-franchise.rationale: The constitution gives every citizen aged eighteen the right to elect and be elected.

property-fundamental.rationale: The constitution denies anyone ownership of the social means of production, caps farmland at ten hectares per household and allows expropriation of private real property in the general interest.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The constitution requires property rights to be exercised in conformity with the social interest and allows expropriation when the general interest requires.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The constitution commits Yugoslavia to the rights of members of Yugoslav nations living as minorities in other countries.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The 1974 constitution guarantees citizens the right to be informed of developments of concern to them, though foreign, religious and nationality policy stayed closed to the press.

public-ownership.rationale: The 1974 constitution makes the means of production social property that no one may own, so industry, energy and transport belonged to society rather than to private owners.

public-service-media.rationale: All media required the political sponsorship of the party-led socialist alliances, and Tanjug guided the handling of controversial topics (Library of Congress study).

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The constitution makes religion a private affair separate from the state.

racial-franchise.rationale: The constitution gives all citizens equal rights to elect and be elected regardless of nationality or race.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The 1958 Programme holds that working people of all nationalities share common interests and combats national and racial prejudice.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The constitution makes citizens equal regardless of race and punishes propagating inequality or racial hatred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The 1958 Programme calls for a scientific, materialist outlook and an ideological struggle against religious and other delusions.

recall-officials.rationale: The 1974 constitution makes every holder of an elected function personally responsible and liable to recall.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The 1974 constitution makes assemblies elected and recallable delegations, and delegates were held to the positions of those who chose them.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Federal funds redistributed investment to the less developed republics, which Slovenes and Croats resented (Library of Congress study).

religion-illusion.rationale: The 1958 Programme says religion springs from material and spiritual backwardness and will be overcome by socialist development and science.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The 1958 Programme names religious ideas among the prejudices still holding back women's equality.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The constitution gives all religious communities the same separate status and freedom to conduct their affairs.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Conscientious objectors were treated harshly and no alternative service was available (Library of Congress study).

religious-nation.rationale: The constitution makes citizens equal regardless of religion, and Yugoslav unity spanned Orthodox, Catholic and Muslim peoples.

religious-offensive-war.rationale: The constitution commits Yugoslavia to a policy against aggression and war.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: The constitution guarantees equal rights to all nations and nationalities living in Yugoslavia.

replace-appointed-officials.rationale: The 1963 constitution's rotation rule limited executive officials to two four-year terms (Library of Congress study).

restore-past-order.rationale: The 1958 Programme treats the prewar order as backward and oppressive and sets socialist transformation as its goal.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The 1974 constitution makes any incitement of national, racial or religious hatred and intolerance unconstitutional and punishable, and 'fostering national hatred' was prosecuted.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes had no legal standing before 1990 and union officials were expected to suppress work stoppages until 1987 (Library of Congress study).

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The constitution commits Yugoslavia to equality in world economic relations and to conditions for the faster development of underdeveloped countries.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Tito told the 1957 workers' councils congress that self-management needed no theoretical justification because its results proved it, and the Programme rejects turning any method into a dogma.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The 1958 Programme seeks modern industry and large-scale scientific agriculture to raise living standards.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Yugoslavia lent heavily to poorer nonaligned countries, losing much money in unrepaid loans (Library of Congress study).

right-to-secede.rationale: The 1974 constitution founds Yugoslavia on each nation's right to self-determination including secession, but the regime purged and arrested the Croatian movement that sought near-independence in 1971.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The 1958 Programme treats the village as backward and expects modern farming to bring peasants a more civilized, urban-like way of life.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The 1958 Programme makes Marxist materialism the League's outlook and treats religion as a delusion.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The 1958 Programme condemns the ignorant, sectarian underestimation of the cultural heritage, which socialist society accepts and cultivates.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The 1958 Programme makes Marxist materialism its outlook and treats religion as a delusion.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The 1974 constitution makes any arbitrary act violating rights punishable whoever commits it and entitles victims of unlawful state action to damages.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The regime relied heavily on Western aid and loans, which covered much of its trade deficit through the 1950s (Library of Congress study).

separate-church-state.rationale: The 1974 constitution declares religious communities separate from the state and religion a private affair, and the 1958 Programme backs separation of church from state and school from church.

separated-powers.rationale: Titoist doctrine held to the unity of power in the assembly, leaving courts unable to review federal laws in the 1950s, and even the later federal Constitutional Court could only refer its findings to the Federal Assembly (McVicker; Library of Congress study).

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: A 1969 resolution on family planning stressed the role of social services and other institutions in sex education and planned parenthood (Library of Congress study).

shared-marital-authority.rationale: After the war women won complete civil and political rights, ending interwar laws that kept them subservient in the family (Library of Congress study).

single-official-language.rationale: The constitution guarantees the equal use of each nation's and nationality's language before state agencies and in schooling.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The regime kept the Albanians of Kosovo and western Macedonia in separate units and made autonomous provinces within Serbia (Library of Congress study).

smash-state-machine.rationale: The 1958 Programme praises the Yugoslav revolution for razing the old political system but allows that elsewhere the working class may rise to power through parliamentary means.

social-market-economy.rationale: Market socialism combined market exchange with social ownership and social protection, rejecting both laissez-faire and central command (Library of Congress study).

socialism-needs-revolutionary-war.rationale: The 1958 Programme holds that some countries can reach socialism by comparatively peaceful means.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The 1958 Programme holds that each country builds socialism by its own road and that peaceful coexistence, not revolution abroad, best advances it.

socialized-care.rationale: The 1958 Programme seeks to free the family from backward housekeeping through public services and children's institutions, while calling the family's role irreplaceable.

socialized-markets.rationale: Yugoslavia's market socialism combined market exchange with enterprises that were socially owned and managed by their workers (Library of Congress study).

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Refusing military service in wartime was punishable by five years in prison up to death (Library of Congress study).

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The constitution makes arbitrary acts punishable regardless of who commits them and binds everyone to the constitution and law.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The 1958 Programme counts the Soviet Union among the socialist countries, criticising its Stalinist bureaucratic deformations rather than calling it capitalist.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The 1958 Programme defines every state by its class substance, bourgeois democracy as the framework of capitalist rule, and Yugoslavia's as a dictatorship of the proletariat.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The state kept control of investment allocation in the 1950s, but the 1965 reform limited it and the 1974 constitution virtually ended direct federal investment (Library of Congress study).

state-finances-worker-businesses.rationale: In the 1950s the state kept control of investment resources allocated to self-managed enterprises (Library of Congress study).

state-harmful.rationale: Self-management doctrine held that the state would eventually disappear as self-managing organizations took over its functions, but the regime kept the state and its security organs in the meantime (Library of Congress study).

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Secularization followed government modernization programmes and vigorous antireligious propaganda (Library of Congress study).

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The 1958 Programme attacks Stalin's theory of a state that does not wither away but must strengthen itself as a revision of Marxism.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Nonalignment between East and West was the keystone of Yugoslav foreign policy from the 1950s (Library of Congress study).

strong-leader.rationale: Tito was the final arbiter of the deadlocks between factions, and the constitution let the assembly elect him president for an unlimited term (Library of Congress study).

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The regime took church land, closed church schools and imprisoned clergy, and kept pressure on religious communities until the 1980s (Library of Congress study).

suppress-opposition.rationale: The regime imprisoned Djilas and other dissidents, silenced the Praxis group in 1975 and disbanded Matica Hrvatska (Library of Congress study).

surveillance-ok.rationale: The secret police kept a dense network of informers and surveillance, curbed after 1951 but kept as an instrument of control, and the constitution did not protect communications from police interference (McVicker; Library of Congress study).

taxation-theft.rationale: The 1974 constitution binds everyone to contribute, in proportion to their means, to general social needs.

term-limits.rationale: The 1963 constitution introduced rotation, barring anyone from executive posts for more than two four-year terms, Tito excepted (Library of Congress study).

territorial-expansion.rationale: The 1958 Programme calls the very idea of changing frontiers by force alien to the League, and the army a force for peace without aggressive character.

torture-always-illegal.rationale: The constitution guarantees the integrity of the person and makes extortion of a confession punishable.

total-state.rationale: After 1950 the regime moved away from Stalinist state domination of the economy and society, though the party kept political control (Library of Congress study).

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The 1958 Programme calls fascism the most reactionary force of the age while counting itself and the Soviet bloc among the socialist forces.

trade-surplus.rationale: The 1958 Programme aims to reach and keep an even balance of payments with foreign countries.

traditional-family.rationale: The 1958 Programme credits socialism with abolishing patriarchal family legislation and freeing the family from backward housekeeping, and looks to new family relations based on love and comradeship.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The regime instituted civil marriage and secular family and education law for all, and the constitution makes citizens equal regardless of religion (Library of Congress study).

unions-good.rationale: The Confederation of Trade Unions had a constitutional mandate to protect workers' rights and the self-management system, though it was party-dominated and had no adversarial role (Library of Congress study).

universal-healthcare.rationale: The 1974 constitution entitles everyone to health care, and the state ran a public health insurance system whose coverage rose from a quarter of the population in 1952 to over 80 percent by 1984 (Library of Congress study).

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Tito alone could be elected president for an unlimited term, while the 1963 rotation rule barred others from more than two four-year terms in executive office.

vanguard-party.rationale: The 1974 constitution makes the League of Communists the leading organized ideological and political force of the working class.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The 1958 Programme says bourgeois democracy rests on capitalist ownership and warns that wide income gaps create material privileges.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Private enterprise was officially disfavoured and confined to small farms, crafts and shops, while the means of production were social property (Library of Congress study).

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The constitution binds everyone to exercise conscientiously the self-management and public functions entrusted to them.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The 1958 Programme says women's equality is held back by economic underdevelopment and private property relations, to be overcome by socialist development.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The constitution guarantees inheritance and makes citizens equal in rights regardless of sex.

women-suffrage.rationale: The constitution gives all citizens over eighteen, regardless of sex, the right to elect and be elected.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The constitution says whoever is fit but will not work shall not enjoy the rights due on account of labour, while assistance goes to those unable to work.

worker-farmer-alliance.rationale: The 1958 Programme defines Yugoslav government as the alliance of the working class with the other working people, peasants included.

worker-ownership.rationale: Enterprises were owned by society, not by their workers: the constitution forbids any group, workers' collectives included, from holding ownership rights over social resources, and workers had no ownership rights in the assets they managed (Library of Congress study).

workers-councils.rationale: The 1974 constitution built every assembly up from delegations of workplaces and local communities, which the leadership called direct workers' democracy, while keeping a Federal Assembly at the top (Library of Congress study).

workers-nation.rationale: The 1958 Programme defends each party's own national road and Yugoslav socialist patriotism while upholding proletarian internationalism.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Workers' councils elected by all workers set business policy, approved accounts and confirmed directors, as the constitution and the 1950 law required.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The 1958 Programme says the division of the world into industrial powers and backward raw-material producers persists, upheld by new forms of neocolonial dependence.

missingStatements.text: Newly independent and developing countries should stay out of the military blocs of the great powers.
missingStatements.rationale: Non-alignment was a pillar of Titoist foreign policy, and Tito co-founded the Non-Aligned Movement in 1961 and was its first secretary-general.

missingStatements.text: Nationalism that threatens the unity of a multinational state should be legally prosecuted.
missingStatements.rationale: Brotherhood and unity was enforced by convictions of nationalists, and Tito purged nationalism that threatened the federation.

missingStatements.text: State ownership of the means of production should give way to direct ownership by society as a whole.
missingStatements.rationale: Titoism defines itself against Soviet state ownership: Tito called state ownership the lowest form of social ownership, and the 1958 Programme sets the course from state ownership toward direct social ownership managed by the associated producers.

quotes.text: State ownership is the lowest form of social ownership, and not the highest as the leaders of the USSR consider it to be.

The form of socialization of the means of production may be different in the course of development from indirect social, or state, ownership (which is characteristic of the first phase of social development) toward maximum direct social ownership
quotes.where: Programme, ch. VI, 'The Forms and Role of Social Ownership'

notes: Later pass (rules 5) by claude-opus-5-5. The first pass rested almost wholly on Wikipedia; this pass rebuilt it from the 1958 Programme of the League of Yugoslav Communists, the 1974 constitution, Tito's speeches (1950, 1954, 1957, the 1960 UN address) and Kardelj's Socialism and War, with the regime's record from the Library of Congress country study (1990) and McVicker's 1957 study of the 1950s reforms, and Benson's encyclopedia entry for scope. Record over words: where the regime acted (one-party rule, delegate elections, courts, religion policy, media control, conscription, abortion law, prices, trade, nonalignment) the answer rests on the record or the enacted constitution alone; the Programme answers only where there is no record. Over time: the answers follow the mature line of 1950-1980 (self-management, the 1963 and 1974 constitutions), not the Stalinist 1945-48 phase; where the record moved both ways (market socialism after 1965 and Tito's 1974 recentralization, collectivization abandoned while socialist farms were promoted, the constitutional right of secession against the 1971 Croatian purge) the answer is mixed or low. Every first-pass answer was rechecked; 57 that the new sources do not settle are nulled. Not used: Tito's 1956 speech on Hungary (MIA scan without a text layer), and the lending-only archive.org copies of Yugoslavia's Way (the 1958 Programme in another translation) and Neal's Titoism in Action. Themes searched: economy (ownership, planning, markets, prices, unions, strikes, agriculture, taxes, banking, foreign capital), government (party, elections, delegate system, courts, presidency, federation, rotation, recall), liberty (rights chapter, censorship, dissent, surveillance, death penalty), society (religion, family, women, abortion, education, nationalities and languages), world (nonalignment, blocs, UN, colonialism, aid, disarmament, defence doctrine, conscription), ecology and technology (Programme and constitution only).
